why: Accessibility rule 1: primary text and icons reach 4.5:1 on every tone
Accessibility rule 1: dim text reaches 4.5:1 on every tone
Accessibility rule 2: accent reaches 3:1 against every tone it marks (check marks, ticks in menus, block markers, fills on tracks)
Accessibility rule 1: on-accent text reaches 4.5:1 on accent
Accessibility rule 2: a hovered or focused checked toggle is filled with accent hover, which reaches 3:1 against the surface it marks
Accessibility rule 1: on-danger text and icons reach 4.5:1 on danger; text on danger does not
Accessibility rule 5: the window outline tells a window from the one behind it, at 2:1 against the tones of a window (D-62). It is not measured against the window glow.
Accessibility rule 4: the focused tone stands apart from the widget at rest and from the surface. 1.2 is a floor that keeps the focused tone from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-77).
Accessibility rule 4: the focused tone of a tab or a scroll area stands apart from the tab bar and from the surface. 1.2 is a floor that keeps the focused tone from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-77).
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an empty well is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is a floor that keeps the step from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-75, D-77).

Accessibility rule 2: the mark of a disabled checked toggle and the fill of a disabled slider or progress bar are dim text, and still mark state (P3.5). A tick mark of a slider is dim text on the surface, covered by dim text on tone-2.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an unchecked toggle is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is a floor that keeps the step from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-75, D-77).

Accessibility, departure from WCAG: a hovered well or unchecked toggle is told by tone from a dialog's tone 1 body, where it vanished, and from the toggle at rest (D-102, D-106). On tone 2 it measures 1.11:1, which the owner accepted in D-102; a pair there would sit within 2 % of the floor. 1.1 is a floor that keeps the step from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-77).
Accessibility rule 4: the focused tone stands apart from the widget at rest and from the surface. 1.2 is a floor that keeps the focused tone from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-77).
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an empty track is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is a floor that keeps the step from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-75, D-77).
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: the thumb of a slider or a scrollbar is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is a floor that keeps the step from fading, not a WCAG rule (D-75, D-77).
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: a hovered thumb is told from its surface by tone, as the thumb at rest is.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: a pressed thumb is told from its surface by tone, as the thumb at rest is.
Accessibility rule 4: a bar at the foot of a focused well marks state, so it reaches 3:1 on the well and on the surface. It is the focus cue of a well, whose tone stays below the surface (D-69).
A selected item is told by its tone alone, with no block marker (D-111). 1.1 is a floor that keeps the tone from fading (my call).

Folder icons take the colour scheme's Selection background, which is this token (D-110): a folder stays apart from the view, a sidebar and a selected or focused item. 1.1 is a floor (my call); the icon's own shading does the rest.

The text selection is told from the editor and the current line by tone and hue; its text carries the 4.5:1. 1.1 is a floor that keeps it from fading (my call).
